content:
Yes, when you run `pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>`, it will delete the entire virtual environment including all the packages installed in it.

The command removes the entire directory structure of the virtual environment, which includes:
- The Python interpreter copy
- All installed packages in the `site-packages` directory
- Any scripts or binaries in the `bin` directory
- Configuration files

So all pip-installed packages specific to that virtual environment will be completely removed. This is actually one of the benefits of using virtual environments - you can cleanly remove all associated packages by simply deleting the environment.

If you want to preserve a list of installed packages before deletion, you can first export them:
```bash
pyenv activate <venv-name>
pip freeze > requirements.txt
```

This way you can recreate the environment later with the same packages using:
```bash
pyenv virtualenv <python-version> <new-venv-name>
pyenv activate <new-venv-name>
pip install -r requirements.txt
```
